blocks.passage:
Sanctions are rules that stop companies from doing business with certain countries, people or products. They are set by governments and international bodies for political or legal reasons.

The rules can be strict. You cannot sell certain products to a country on the list. You must not send money to certain names. The fines are very big, and the damage to the company's name can be even bigger.

The safe answer is simple: if you are not sure, ask — and always check the list first.

items.q: What do sanctions do?
options: Stop companies from doing business with certain countries, people or products
items.why: "Sanctions are rules that stop companies from doing business with certain countries, people or products."

items.q: Who sets sanctions?
items.why: "They are set by governments and international bodies."

items.q: According to the text, what can you not do?
options: Sell certain products to a listed country or send money to certain names
items.why: "You cannot sell certain products to a country on the list. You must not send money to certain names."

items.q: Besides big fines, what else can be damaged?
items.why: "the damage to the company's name can be even bigger."

items.q: What is the safe answer?
options: If you are not sure, ask — and always check the list first
items.why: "if you are not sure, ask — and always check the list first."

audio.text:
I need to explain why we cannot ship our usual product to this new customer, even though it looks like a normal order. The reason is sanctions.

This customer is in a country that is currently on a restricted list. That means governments have said: you must not sell certain products there. Our product is one of them.

I know it feels frustrating. The customer seems friendly, the order is good, the money looks real. But it doesn't matter how good the deal is. If it breaks a sanction, we cannot do it. Full stop.

And this isn't a small thing. The fines for breaking sanctions are enormous — far more than any single order is worth. And worse, our company's name would be damaged. Banks and partners would stop trusting us. That can take years to repair.

So the rule for everyone here is simple and firm: before any deal with a new country or name, we check the sanctions list first. If something is on the list, or if you're not sure, you stop and ask me. Never guess with sanctions.

items.why: "This customer is in a country that is currently on a restricted list."

items.q: **Sanctions** are…
options: rules that stop business with certain countries, people or products
items.why: Sanctions = sanções.

items.q: A **watchlist** is…
options: a list of restricted names or parties to check against
items.why: Watchlist = lista de vigilância.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Breaking the rules can bring a huge **___**."
items.why: Fine = multa.

items.q: To **screen** a name means to…
options: check it against a restricted list
items.why: Screen = checar/triar.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "That product is **___** for this country."
items.why: Forbidden = proibido.

items.q: "If it breaks a sanction, we cannot do it. **Full stop**." Full stop here means…
items.why: Full stop = ponto final, sem exceção.

items.q: "Always **check the list** first." To check the list means to…
options: look at it to be sure
items.why: Check the list = conferir a lista.

items.q: "Never **guess** with sanctions." To guess means to…
items.why: Guess = chutar, agir sem certeza.

items.q: "Trust can **take years to repair**." To repair here means to…
items.why: Repair = reparar, reconstruir.

items.q: "If you're not sure, **stop and ask**." This advises you to…
items.why: Stop and ask = parar e perguntar.
